# Drivetrain on carpet (auto-generated by `python -m rnd.run_all`)

Robot + 2 kg payload = **21.2 kg**; 4 × 6" omni wheels (r = 76 mm) direct-driven by GIM6010-8 (5 N·m rated / 11 N·m peak, 120 rpm rated). Layout: **4-wheel, one wheel pointing forward**, holonomic.

## Rolling resistance

| Carpet | Crr (ESTIMATE) | Total force | Torque per driven wheel | Power at 0.8 m/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| low pile | 0.05 | 10.4 N | 0.40 N·m (2 wheels driving forward) | 8 W |
| medium pile | 0.1 | 20.8 N | 0.79 N·m (2 wheels driving forward) | 17 W |

## Thresholds (wheel load ≈ 52 N)

| Step | Push needed per wheel | Torque if the wheel climbs head-on | Torque at 45° heading | vs 5 N·m rated |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 mm | 20 N | 1.51 N·m | 2.14 N·m | ✅ |
| 10 mm | 30 N | 2.26 N·m | 3.20 N·m | ✅ |
| 15 mm | 39 N | 2.94 N·m | 4.16 N·m | ✅ |
| 20 mm | 48 N | 3.63 N·m | 5.13 N·m | ⚠️ peak |

**Catch:** a wheel rolling *sideways* meets the step with its small rollers (~25 mm, ESTIMATE). It can't climb more than a few mm on its own; the other wheels have to drag it over.
**Rule for the planner:** cross thresholds at a **45° heading**, so every wheel uses its full diameter. That needs ≤ 4.2 N·m per wheel for 15 mm, within rating. **Must be bench-tested** (Phase-1 base test); fallback is 8" dual-row omni wheels (bigger rollers).

## Speed and acceleration

- Forward speed at rated motor speed: **0.96 m/s** (2 side wheels drive straight); at 45° heading 0.68 m/s. Max motor speed allows ~3.4 m/s. R6 (0.8 m/s) ✅
- Motor-limited acceleration: 12.4 m/s². Traction-limited (μ ≈ 0.6): 5.9 m/s².
- **Stability-limited** (twin v0): 1.4–1.6 m/s² with the arm at full high reach. **Controller limits: 1.0 m/s² with arms parked, 0.5 m/s² while manipulating.**

## Odometry on carpet

Wheel counts are unreliable on carpet (rollers slip and sink), so position comes from:
1. a **PAA5100JE optical-flow** sensor, 15–35 mm above the floor, in the base centre
2. **IMU** yaw
3. **RPLIDAR C1** scan matching
4. wheel counts, used only as a weak prior

All fused in an EKF. Bench test: sensor height vs pile depth.
